competitive_landscape: Trasmediterránea and Baleària run the inter-island and mainland ro-ro/fast-ferry trunks. Within Menorca, water transport is fragmented seasonal day-tripper boats. None operates an electric / foiling tier — the UNESCO Biosphere positioning actively favours a quiet-mode entrant. Mallorca↔Menorca is the cleanest competitive opening: short, busy, and currently diesel-only.

precedents.why_it_matters: Mallorca↔Menorca is the cleanest existing eastward extension. Treat as 'extend the Balearics cluster' rather than standalone — the Pioneer II spoke wires Menorca straight into the existing atlas spine.

regulatory_note: Med SOx-ECA + FuelEU Maritime apply. Spain's Balearic tourism-cap politics are increasingly aggressive — registration caps on charter and rental boats and tightening cruise quotas at Palma — favouring high-utilisation, low-impact electric foiling. The entire island is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve (MAB programme), which is the cleanest single-document quiet-mode anchor in the Western Med.
seasonality: Summer peak (June–September) with the population doubling to ~160k; shoulder months May and October work for the coastal spine. Winter operations thin out sharply on Menorca, more than Mallorca. The island sits in the lee of Mallorca for the prevailing west — the Mallorca↔Menorca spoke is generally workable through the shoulder season.

summary: Menorca is the quiet third Balearic. The airport handled ~4.0M passengers in 2023 and the island more than doubles its ~100k resident population in August (~160k visitors), yet it stays calmer and more conservation-led than the built Ibiza and Mallorca nodes: the entire island is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, layering a clean island-wide quiet-mode lever on top of the Med SOx-ECA and the Balearic tourism caps. Mahón is one of the world's largest natural harbours. Mallorca↔Menorca is ~25 nm — a clean Pioneer II spoke that extends the Balearics cluster eastward rather than a standalone scan.
